name: Gallizenae

attributes.attribute: were Druid women who lived off Brittany on the Isle de Sena
formed a college of priestesses like the one that served the Irish Brigit

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Gallizenae were Breton folkloric figures. They were Druid women. They lived off the west coast of Brittany on the Isle de Seine. The isle lies near Pointe de Raz. They connect to the tales of the dissolute princess Dahut and her city of Ys. They formed a college of priestesses. The college resembled the one that served the Irish Brigit. They practiced divination and other magic without contact with men.

okr.objective: Record the Gallizenae as Druid women of Breton legend.
key_results: Place the Gallizenae on the Isle de Sena near Pointe de Raz.
Describe them as a college of priestesses linked to the Irish Brigit.
State their practice of divination and magic apart from men.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2008, s.v. 'Gallizenae'.
